races.name: Betfred Champagne Trial EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Betfred St Leger Trial Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: According To Mark
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 1m2f on Good ground for Edward Bethell and Tudhope, stepping up to 1m4f here which looks a logical progression, though his style is uncertain and he has yet to win in four starts; 37 days off is not a concern on this ground.

runners_data.name: Brave Hunter
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has found his feet over 1m2f-1m4f on Good, and the step back up in trip with Kevin Stott aboard suits his prominent style; headgear worn previously and Ismail Mohammed's yard is out of form (0 from 5 in 14 days), which is a mild flag.

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up operator has a solid placed record over 1m2f on Good ground, and 55 days off could mean he arrives fresh and forward; this is his first run at 1m4f so the extra two furlongs is an unknown quantity, though his staying profile suggests it will suit.

runners_data.name: Count Bezukhov
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's charge carries top weight but boasts the highest class credentials in the field with a win at 1m2f on Good and a third over 1m4f, and Billy Loughnane steering him from a prominent pitch is a compelling combination; his OR of 120 towers over most rivals.

runners_data.name: Shoof Baeed
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner won his only start over 1m2f on Good and maps as the lone front-runner, but the STYLE_FIT flag notes he is racing somewhat out of role; if he settles and controls the pace he remains a force, but his chance is tempered if the race shape does not suit his natural running.

runners_data.name: Poker
runners_data.note: David Egan takes the ride on this K. R. Burke hold-up type who has twice finished second over 1m2f and 1m4f on Good ground, and the step up in class here against OR-120 rivals is a significant ask; needs the pace to genuinely collapse in the straight to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Saifo
runners_data.note: David Simcock's lightly raced runner is an unknown quantity — no days-since-last-run data, no form string, and going experience is uncertain; Sean Levey's booking for a horse at OR 120 warrants respect, but there is simply insufficient data to map his likely role.

runners_data.name: Sea And Sun
runners_data.note: The second Charlie Johnston runner has placed twice on Good ground over 1m2f-1m4f and is lightly raced, so retains improvement potential; Rowan Scott takes over at 130lbs and with only 10 days between runs he arrives fresh, though his style is unconfirmed over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Shoof Baeed is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he will dictate at whatever tempo suits him — almost certainly a measured, controlled gallop given the trip and his lone-leader status. Count Bezukhov and Brave Hunter sit prominently behind him, meaning the race will have a clear shape from the outset: a single leader, two attendants close up, and the hold-up horses — Hatteen and Poker — operating from the rear. On Good to Firm ground over 1m4f at Doncaster's straight, flat track, an uncontested pace typically rewards the leader or the horse closest to the pace who can respond when the tempo lifts in the straight. The race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers who need a strong gallop to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Shoof Baeed sets a comfortable, uncontested pace and the field fails to produce a meaningful challenge until the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Shoof Baeed controls every yard from the front on Good to Firm ground over 1m4f with no pressure, conserving energy before asserting in the Doncaster straight; a sustainable tempo means the race is run entirely to his terms and the prominent horses tracking him are best placed to exploit any crack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Shoof Baeed's pace is sufficient to string the field out but a prominent racer improves to lead inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Count Bezukhov, with the class edge and one win already at 1m2f on Good ground, is ideally placed to track and pounce, while Brave Hunter pressing close from a prominent position could also grab the prize as the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely strong enough to flatten the leaders and a midfield mover picks them off late.
scenarios.body: Hatteen has finished second twice over 1m2f on Good ground and stepping up in trip could help him sustain his finish longer; similarly, According To Mark has placed prominently over shorter trips and a strong gallop at this distance could bring him into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp A Slow Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the hold-up horses produce an unexpected late flourish.
scenarios.body: Poker has shown ability to place over 1m4f on Good ground and could benefit from a muddled finish, while Hatteen's hold-up style gives him a closing profile; however, Doncaster's flat, undemanding straight rarely gifts closers a strong enough pace collapse to overcome well-positioned rivals.

watchPoints.text: Count Bezukhov holds clear class superiority at OR 120 with proven form over 1m2f-1m4f on Good ground and Billy Loughnane tracking the lone leader — watch him as the most dangerous prominent horse to pounce in the straight.

Shoof Baeed carries the STYLE_FIT flag — if he fails to settle comfortably in front or is pressured earlier than expected, his ability to control the race dissolves and the scenario probabilities shift sharply toward Count Bezukhov.

Saifo is a complete unknown with no publicly available form or going data despite carrying OR 120 — Sean Levey's booking suggests potential, and punters should monitor market moves as a proxy for stable confidence.
Brave Hunter's trainer combination is 0-from-5 in the past 14 days, a mild negative angle worth tracking if his price tightens without obvious justification in the market.

The Good to Firm ground at Doncaster is firmer than the declared Good — horses with a preference for genuinely Good ground (Hatteen, Poker, Brave Hunter all have soft-ground form) may find conditions quicker than ideal, marginally favouring those with confirmed Good to Firm or fast-ground winners.

races.name: Betfred Supports Jack Berry House Handicap

runners_data.name: Lordsbridge Grey
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Stuart Woods who has shown some ability on good ground at shorter trips, stepping up to 1m6½f for the first time here; five recent runs show zero wins and just one place at comparable conditions, and being forced to close from rear in a race Tazaman controls tempo on is not an easy ask at this trip on first attempt.

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 1m6f trip on good ground at her latest start — that form is the standout recent evidence in the field — but by nature she wants to be held up late, and with four rivals ahead of her in a slowly run race, that closing run may not materialise with the force it did last time; Zoe Lewis takes a 7lb claim which softens the weight.

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's four-year-old has three places from seven runs on good ground and is unexposed over this 1m6f-plus trip, giving Aiden Brookes a horse with genuine each-way claims if the pace sets up for a staying finish; 17 days since last run is straightforward, though a question mark sits over her form at the top of the distance range.

runners_data.name: Tazaman
runners_data.note: Kevin and Lauren Frost's nine-year-old is the only confirmed pace-setter and will get an uncontested lead on good-to-firm Doncaster ground — she has placed in seven of fifteen similar-going runs and her last four outings over 1m2f-1m4f show consistent form; stepping to 1m6½f is the key stamina query, but a solo lead with no pressure is a significant tactical advantage for Joanna Mason to exploit.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by inclination but has been moved forward on the pace map due to the cluster of closers in the field; Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking, though the horse's recent record reads 3-8-0-7-3 with no wins and limited impact on good ground, and being asked to race in a more prominent role than natural would be against her best form tendencies.

races.paceDynamic: Tazaman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and will stride into the lead from the off over 1m6½f on good-to-firm ground at Doncaster, setting what is expected to be a measured, uncontested gallop with no rival likely to press for supremacy. The remaining four runners — Lordsbridge Grey, Golden Flame, Twilight Safari, and Nanny Park — all carry hold-up profiles, meaning Tazaman faces zero pressure and can control tempo entirely to suit herself. On a flat, galloping track like Doncaster over this stamina trip, an uncontested leader dictating a sustainable pace is a formidable tactical position, and the hold-up horses will need to find meaningful late momentum from well off the pace. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/front-running profile: Tazaman can conserve energy, pick up when ready, and make it very difficult for hold-up horses to reel her in from a standing start at the business end. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Golden Flame and Nanny Park are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield on the map; in practice, Billy Loughnane on Nanny Park and the connections of Golden Flame may try to sit closer than their usual style, but Tazaman is most likely to secure and hold the front position throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tazaman Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tazaman bowls into the lead uncontested and controls the gallop throughout on good-to-firm ground.
scenarios.body: Joanna Mason settles Tazaman in front at her own pace, conserving enough to repel late challengers on the long Doncaster straight; the hold-up horses face too much ground to make up against a relaxed leader who has never been pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Tazaman sets a stronger-than-expected gallop early and ties herself up in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get a genuine target to aim at and the extended trip exposes any stamina limitation in Tazaman, allowing the closers to pick up ground down the straight; Golden Flame, who won over this exact trip on good ground last time, is best placed to capitalise given her proven stamina profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves truly crawling and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the field and removes Tazaman's stamina advantage, turning it into a sharp tactical contest; Twilight Safari, who has shown positional speed over 1m6f-1m7f on good ground with three placings in similar conditions, is the most likely beneficiary of a kick-for-home scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tazaman overcooks the fractions early under front-runner pressure from a hold-up horse attempting to take her on.
scenarios.body: An atypical race shape where genuine hold-up horses have moved forward to contest pace sees the race blow up late, handing a significant advantage to whichever closer has hugged the rail and conserved energy; Lordsbridge Grey or Nanny Park could emerge from an attritional finish, though both have limited recent form to support this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Tazaman — watch whether Joanna Mason goes straight to the front or is allowed to drift into a lead: if she leads by two lengths or more inside the first furlong with no challenge, this race is likely to be hers to lose.

Golden Flame — despite the redistribution on the map, her win over this exact trip on good ground last time is the most relevant recent form in the race; watch if Zoe Lewis attempts to sit closer than expected to compensate for the lack of a true pace to close into.

Twilight Safari — three places on good ground over this type of distance make her a quiet threat if the pace drifts and the straight turns into a test of staying stamina; watch her position two furlongs out.

Nanny Park — Billy Loughnane's booking stands out as a jockey upgrade, but watch whether the horse settles in her natural hold-up position or is pushed forward; any sign of keenness early on good-to-firm ground over 1m6½f would be a negative for her staying chance.

Overall field size — with only five runners and one leader, the race is unlikely to develop a strong gallop; watch the early sectionals for signs of a falsely run race that could compress the finish and neutralise Tazaman's positional advantage.

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Big Eagle
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse for Warren Greatrex whose recent form figures of 5-2-9 include a win at Sandown over 8f in good ground; stepping up to 1m2f is a positive angle but he needs a strong pace to be delivered late and the likely controlled tempo here works against him — 66 days off also worth noting.

runners_data.name: Suddenly I See
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Charlie Johnston-trained three-year-old who has won twice in six runs on similar ground and arrives in good recent form (1-1604); naturally prominent, he should secure a comfortable berth tracking Obito and his course form at comparable going reads well for this trip.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's gelding carries headgear and arrives on the back of a win over 10f in good ground, giving him directly relevant form for this trip and conditions; Billy Loughnane takes the ride for a yard that has shown solid recent strike rate, and two wins from seven runs on similar ground underpin his claims off a handy prominent position.

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for David O'Meara who will be allowed a soft lead from the off, though his STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 reminds us he is slightly out of role in this field context; his OR of 80 heads the field and he handles Good ground well (2W7P on similar), but uncontested leaders on Doncaster's straight track can be caught by well-positioned rivals in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer — visored, and with consistent placed efforts at 8f on various surfaces — who has been remapped to midfield here because the field's rear is already occupied; his true nature means he needs to find room late and the likely pace scenario does not set up ideally for a horse whose last five runs show a best of one win from 15 similar-ground attempts.

runners_data.name: Domination
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's three-year-old has won twice recently over 8-10f on soft and good ground and is a natural front-runner at heart, though with several prominent types ahead of him in the positional queue he is mapped to midfield and carries a 0.92 STYLE_FIT discount; his best chance relies on recovering a forward pitch early or profiting from any pace disruption, and his trainer has no recent runners in the formbook.

runners_data.name: Island Bear
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott rides this Richard Newland & Jamie Insole-trained hold-up type whose last five runs are all at 7-8f on soft or standard ground, making both the step up to 1m2f and the Good to Firm conditions untested factors; his form figures of 36-754 offer little encouragement for a race likely to be run at a controlled tempo that brings closers up short.

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon's mount won over 10f on good ground earlier in his career and so the trip is not unfamiliar, but this William Knight-trained three-year-old is a genuinely prominent-racing type forced off his natural position by the congestion ahead of him; his last four runs include a last-place finish and a seventh, and with the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 and his true front-running nature compromised, his prospects in a race dominated by Obito are limited.

races.paceDynamic: Obito is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to push for the lead from the outset, he should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster. Suddenly I See and Room Fourteen are the natural prominent types best placed to track him from positions two and three, giving them a clear line through the race. This field contains more pace-minded runners than the map can accommodate — Domination and Brighton View are genuine prominent racers who will struggle to secure their favoured spots and may be forced wider or further back than ideal, while Intrusively is a true hold-up type similarly remapped to midfield. With a single uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace on fast ground at a galloping track, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-tracking types who can travel into the race and produce a sustained finish in the straight rather than those reliant on a truly-run race generating a late sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Obito Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Obito bowls along at a fair but unexaggerated pace and the prominent brigade track him through the race
scenarios.body: Obito's uncontested lead on Good to Firm ground at Doncaster sets an even tempo that suits those able to travel close to the pace, with the straight giving Room Fourteen and Suddenly I See the room to pick up and reel him in; both have strong recent form at this trip and in similar conditions, making them the prime beneficiaries

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and Obito steals enough of a buffer that the closers cannot close the gap in time
scenarios.body: On quick ground at Doncaster's galloping track an uncontested front-runner can be hard to catch if the early fractions are slow, and Obito's official rating of 80 gives him a legitimate chance of lasting home if pursers are caught flat-footed; his STYLE_FIT tag warrants a discount but the scenario is real if the tempo is falsely slow

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Held-Up Type Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions prove fast enough to string the field out and create genuine end-to-end pace
scenarios.body: Big Eagle and Island Bear are the truest hold-up horses in this field and would need a strong gallop to generate the momentum for a late run over 1m2f; with only one confirmed front-runner and a likely regulated tempo, this scenario depends on pace developing organically from the prominent battle and is therefore less probable

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Pace, Chaos Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of prominent types causes early jostling and an uneven tempo that scrambles the anticipated race shape
scenarios.body: Domination and Brighton View, both natural prominent types unable to secure their preferred positions, may create unexpected early pressure as they seek to recover ground, potentially setting a faster pace than Obito wants and opening the door to an opportunist; this is a low-probability shape but could benefit Domination if he manages to assert from a wide tracking position

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Domination and Brighton View, both natural prominent types, attempt to press forward from the off — if either forces an early positional battle with Obito the pace could accelerate unexpectedly and alter the entire race shape.

Obito's STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 means his ability to control this from the front in an unaccustomed role should not be taken for granted; if he is headed or pressed before halfway his chance diminishes sharply.

Room Fourteen's headgear entry is worth monitoring in the paddock — if he is equipped with a hood or blindfold for the first time it could affect his early behaviour and his ability to slot in smoothly behind the leader.

Suddenly I See ran just 12 days ago, the shortest turnaround in this field; Connor Beasley should know the horse well for Charlie Johnston but watch for any signs of a quick-return effect in the paddock or at the start.

Big Eagle and Island Bear are the only two genuine hold-up horses in this race by natural style; if the pace is truly uncontested and slow, backers of either should be aware that neither has the profile to benefit from anything other than a strongly-run contest.

races.name: Betfred Nifty 50 Handicap (Rnd)

runners_data.name: Kiss Me My Love
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer who has won and placed over this exact 8f trip on Good, with a sharp recent form line including a course win; Joanna Mason keeps her close enough to the pace in smaller fields to be ideally placed here, and 36 days off is not a concern given that prep.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with consistent form at 10f on Good, though the step back to a mile is a slight query; P J McDonald rides and she has headgear noted, but her true style is deep hold-up and she has been mapped forward simply because the field is saturated with closers — her chance depends on the pace being stronger than expected.

runners_data.name: Norcross Brow
runners_data.note: Won a 7f Good race last time out and shaped well at this trip before, though soft-ground efforts earlier muddy the picture; Charlie Clover has a solid 14-day strike and Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking, yet this is a genuine closer who has been pushed into midfield on the map rather than his natural position at the rear — 9 days between runs is tight for a three-year-old.

runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the central tactical figure in this race; equipped with a hood, Harry Vigors claims 5lb, and the step up to a mile from his recent 7f runs opens a slight stamina question, but on a flat Doncaster track with no one to press him the controlled conditions may mask that concern.

runners_data.name: Celtic Chariot
runners_data.note: Three-year-old whose four-run form string shows a place at 7f Good and a near-miss at 8f Good, making this trip and going a reasonable fit; David Egan is a strong jockey booking for Kevin & Lauren Frost who have shown two wins from 18 runs over 14 days, and Celtic Chariot is one of the more naturally forward of the hold-up group which helps in this pace shape.

runners_data.name: Myrrh
runners_data.note: David O'Meara runner with a strong trainer strike rate (7/59) and Daniel Tudhope — one of the shrewdest pace-readers in the north — in the saddle, which counts for something; form is over 10-12f and this mile trip looks short, and the horse's deep hold-up style has been redistributed forward on the map purely by field composition rather than any tactical adjustment.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has not registered a win or place on Good or faster in five comparable starts; equipped with a hood, Rowan Scott rides for the Newland/Insole combination who show three wins from 30 over 14 days, but zero good-going placed efforts is a damaging flag and the redistribution forward on the map does not reflect this horse's genuine tactical preference.

races.paceDynamic: Okiru is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no rival likely to contest the lead aggressively, should secure a comfortable, uncontested lead through the first half of this Doncaster mile on Good to Firm ground. The pace is therefore expected to be honest but controlled rather than searingly strong, as Okiru sets the tempo without being pressured — a pattern that historically suits those who can sit just off the pace and quicken from a short distance out rather than those who need a truly searching gallop to close from the rear. Kiss Me My Love, Celtic Chariot, and the cluster of redistributed hold-up types will all be chasing from behind a single front-runner on a galloping track that does not inherently favour deep closers unless the pace is genuinely strong. This race shape — a lone front-runner dictating on Good to Firm going — most clearly favours a prominent or pace-stalking runner who can track Okiru and pounce in the straight, rather than true hold-up horses, several of whom have been pushed forward on the map because the field contains more genuine hold-up types than can all find their natural position; of those, Kiss Me My Love and Celtic Chariot are the most likely to secure a forward enough berth to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Okiru Leads, Pace-Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru leads at a controlled pace and a prominent tracker sits close enough to pounce in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Okiru sets a comfortable gallop and the race sets up for any runner sitting within two or three lengths at the turn, as the moderate pace will not string the field out far enough for a true closer to generate a decisive run from the rear. Good to Firm ground rewards horses who can travel fluently close to the pace rather than those who need a strong tempo to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Off Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru's controlled pace nevertheless creates enough bunching in the final quarter-mile for a well-placed hold-up horse to weave through.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop can still produce a late finishing opportunity if the field compacts in the home straight and gaps appear, but runners tagged as redistributed hold-up types will need to travel closer than their natural style allows. Myrrh or Norcross Brow would be the primary beneficiaries if a pocket materialises, though their style-fit discount makes this a lower-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Okiru Defies Field, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Okiru is allowed such a soft lead that no rival can close the gap from the home turn and the front-runner wins unchallenged.
scenarios.body: With only one genuine pace-setter and a field of hold-up horses, Okiru could exploit the lack of early pressure and build an advantage that proves decisive on the run-in, particularly if rivals are caught flat-footed or wide. Harry Vigors claiming 5lb is a meaningful weight advantage, and Archie Watson runners on Good to Firm are worth noting even at a modest trainer 14-day strike rate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Shuffle, Outsider Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the race unravels tactically with hold-up horses failing to make ground and the field finishing in a heap behind a stopping Okiru.
scenarios.body: An unexpected scenario where pace collapses late and the first finisher emerges from an unpredictable shuffle; the redistributed horses racing out of their natural style create some unpredictability but not enough to raise this probability meaningfully. The Anthony Gover, who has zero wins or places on good-plus going in five similar attempts, is the least likely winner here.

watchPoints.text: Okiru's early gallop is the race-shaper — if Harry Vigors settles into a very slow pace through the first half-mile, the home straight will compress the field into a sprint finish that benefits holders of a prominent position rather than closers.

Kiss Me My Love has the most relevant course and trip form in the field and is ridden by Joanna Mason who tends to position this type boldly — watch for her to travel just off Okiru early, which would give her a decisive positional advantage.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Myrrh, Princess Niyla, Norcross Brow, The Anthony Gover) all need to race closer than their natural style — if they get stuck behind a wall of horses turning for home, the moderate pace will not create the gaps they require.

Norcross Brow is only nine days off his last run for Charlie Clover; monitor the market — if Loughnane's booking reflects stable confidence after that quick turnaround, the three-year-old's recent win form at the trip could make him dangerous despite the style-fit concern.

Good to Firm going is confirmed for this race despite the card listing Good — all runners appear to have form on similar surfaces, but horses with any soft-ground form (Norcross Brow, Myrrh) may find conditions faster than ideal.

races.name: Betfred Play Fred's 5 Million Pound Handicap

runners_data.name: King's School
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in good recent form with a win and a place at 7f on good ground in his last three; Connor Beasley rides and the tinted tongue tie (tp) is a headgear flag worth noting; 27 days off is fine and he wants the race run to suit his late finish.|

runners_data.name: Alpha Capture
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, Roger Fell in decent form (1 win from 6 in last 14 days); won over this exact C&D trip on good ground and has strong course form — an uncontested lead is the key; has raced prominently throughout career.|

runners_data.name: Monsieur Bondy
runners_data.note: Drops in after two poor runs following back-to-back wins at 7f on standard and good; P.J. McDonald is a booking upgrade but the form collapse (10-10) raises questions about current well-being; naturally prominent and will want to be close to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Lord Capulet
runners_data.note: Four wins from 15 starts on good-ish ground and a 7f specialist; Toby Moore's 7lb claim is a big aid at the weights; drew a good recent run at 7f in third, and being prominent suits Doncaster's flat straight.|

runners_data.name: Stanage
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been running over a mile or further of late, dropping back to 7f here; Joanna Mason's record over this trip is limited; course-and-distance form is sparse but the lighter weight (136lbs) after a short 13-day break gives him a fresh profile.|

runners_data.name: Lope El Fuego
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has raced exclusively at 5f-6f until now — the step up to 7f is a key unknown; all five career runs have been on good ground so the surface is no issue; Edward Greatrex takes the ride for his father's yard; 45 days since last run means fitness must be assumed.|

runners_data.name: Bella Bisbee
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on good and has solid each-way form at this trip; naturally a prominent racer but the crowded pace map means she is likely to find herself in a tighter spot than ideal, which blunts her chance given she needs to be rolling from early on.|

runners_data.name: Wrydcroft
runners_data.note: Strong recent form — 1-1-2-3 in last four — all at 7f including three wins or places on good ground; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim helps; a front-running/prominent type by nature but may struggle to assert that role given the competition for those positions in this field.|

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up from 6f; has placed at 6f on good ground but lacks a run at this trip; Billy Loughnane is a high-class booking; 14 days between runs is tight and the step up in trip on a flat track is the key swing factor.|

runners_data.name: Highland Shah
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on good ground last time for Julie Camacho, who is in decent form (3 from 20 in 14 days); worn headgear (h) previously; a prominent type by inclination who will struggle to get to the front in this field and Ryan Sexton will need to adapt his tactics accordingly.|

races.paceDynamic: Alpha Capture is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge from the gun, should secure an uncontested lead at a fair but manageable gallop on this flat Doncaster 7f trip under Kevin Stott. The prominent cluster — Monsieur Bondy, Lord Capulet, and Return Of The Gods — will press close behind, creating a competitive but not frantic early pace that is unlikely to burn Alpha Capture off. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can track the moderate early tempo and unleash a sustained late run into the straight, with King's School and Lope El Fuego the profiles best placed to exploit it. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than the race can accommodate cleanly; Bella Bisbee, Wrydcroft, and Highland Shah are all naturally prominent types but at least one or two will be shuffled back, compromising their chance from the outset.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alpha Capture Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha Capture leads uncontested and sets a fair, unforced gallop that leaves enough in the tank for the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Alpha Capture, untroubled on the front end, controls the tempo throughout and punishes any challengers who have used energy tracking; Roger Fell's runner has won twice at this trip on good ground and a clean lead is its optimal scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just quick enough to stretch the prominent pack, leaving the hold-up brigade with the strongest finish.
scenarios.body: King's School and Lope El Fuego, given their best ground, arrive late down the outside as the front-running pack ties up in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Bella Bisbee, Highland Shah, and Wrydcroft causes a scramble early, inflating the pace and setting things up for one prominent horse who gets a clean split.
scenarios.body: A ragged early order unsettles the prominent pack, but a horse like Lord Capulet or Wrydcroft — if they can fight their way into position — benefits from the resulting strong pace before the turn.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Steals Unnoticed
scenarios.trigger: If no horse takes responsibility early and a compressed field fails to react to a horse creeping into a prominent position from low draw.
scenarios.body: A well-placed runner exploits the traffic, with Stanage or Bella Bisbee benefiting from confusion around them and hitting the line fresh.

watchPoints.text: Alpha Capture's ability to secure the lead uncontested is the single biggest race-shape lever — if anything blasts out to challenge Kevin Stott early, the entire dynamic shifts.|

Bella Bisbee, Highland Shah, and Wrydcroft are all genuine prominent-types mapped back; watch the first two furlongs for a scramble as these three attempt to assert — any collision of intent will inflate the early pace and compromise all three.|
Lope El Fuego has never raced beyond 6f — if the 7f trip proves beyond him in the final quarter-mile, it will be obvious early in the straight and backers should be watching for that fade signal.|

Lord Capulet carries a 7lb claimer in Toby Moore — watch whether Moore settles him in the prominent pack or gets drawn into a pace battle; calm handling early would significantly improve his prospects in the straight.|
King's School is 5-for-1 at 7f on good-to-soft or similar but only 1W from 15 on today's good-to-firm equivalent — the going upgrade is a marginal concern worth monitoring at the off.|

races.name: Betfred Follow Us On X Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Hurt You Never
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with strong 5f form on good ground (15 runs at comparable conditions) and a lively recent run seven days ago, but genuine deep closer whose natural hold-up role is compromised by the sheer number of similar types in this field, likely surfacing from a crowded midfield rather than from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Donald
runners_data.note: Four-year-old fitted with a tongue-tie whose best effort was a 5f second on soft ground; 20 days since last run is fine, but five starts at this trip without a win and the inability to get a true rear-running berth in this field stacks the odds against.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied five-year-old who has raced primarily at 6f-7f and whose best recent placing was a modest fifth at 6f on good; the step down to 5½f and the redistribution out of a genuine closing position both represent meaningful hurdles, and Miss Pippa Brown's 3lb claim is the main upside.

runners_data.name: Koffee And Kale
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win at 5f on soft and a recent placed effort, trained by Michael Bell who is 0W from 24 over the past fortnight; the horse holds genuine form credentials at the trip but has been most effective with cut underfoot, and good-to-firm may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who has been in sparkling form, winning at 6f on good and placing twice at 6f on similar; steps down to 5½f which remains untested but the prominent tracking style suits this pace shape perfectly, and Mr Eireann Cagney should secure an ideal position behind Dicko The Legend.

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has won and placed at 5f on artificial surfaces but has run only three times on turf with modest returns; 97 days since last start is the longest layoff in the field, and while the horse carries the hold-up profile, being genuinely out of role in a bunched midfield represents a significant disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Archie Watson who is 2W from 33 over 14 days — active but not red-hot; won at 6f on good ten days ago and showed a 6f hat-trick of minor finishes before that, suggesting the 5½f is marginal, though the hold-up style in a congested midfield is the bigger concern.

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: Three-year-old fitted with a tongue-tie who has placed at 5f and 6f on good ground in recent starts; Miss Venetia Thompson's 7lb claim is the main tactical attraction, but the horse is a true closer racing out of its natural position in a field saturated with similar types.

runners_data.name: Saucy Jane
runners_data.note: Top weight at 157lbs but the joint-highest OR in the race at 70; has two wins at 6f on good and has placed at 5f, making this trip viable, and the hold-up style is genuine rather than redistributed — Mr Henry Callan should be able to find a clear run if midfield traffic allows.

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in this field and the pivotal horse for the pace shape; has recorded wins and placed efforts at 6f but steps down to 5½f, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild discount, yet in a race with no rival willing to press, Miss Amy Collier can dictate completely.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old has an outstanding recent strike rate for his trainer (15W from 90 in 14 days) and is a genuine hold-up performer with consistent 5f form on good — three placed efforts in his last five at the trip; Mr Thomas Easterby's 3lb claim aids the weight, and this horse is best-equipped of the closers to find a clean passage late.

races.paceDynamic: Dicko The Legend is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 5½f handicap and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outside, should stride into a clear, uncontested lead from the gates and control every yard of a true but not suicidal gallop on good-to-firm ground. Bayraat is the only other horse with a prominent profile and will likely track Dicko The Legend in second, while the remainder of this field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types who will bunch in the middle and rear sections, creating a convoy shape rather than a pressured race. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the track can accommodate in genuine late positions — Hurt You Never, Dorney Lake, Donald, Mister Moet, Lieutenant Sir, and Powernap are all natural closers, but with so many competing for the same space they will be shuffled into midfield roles where they cannot replicate their best form; of those, Spirit Of Applause and Saucy Jane, with cleaner hold-up profiles and relevant form, are best-placed to find the clearest late run. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a controlled, front-running or prominent-tracking shape suits this race, and horses that can sit just behind Dicko The Legend on a fair pace and produce a sustained finish will have the decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dicko Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dicko The Legend secures an uncontested lead and the pack fails to close the gap quickly enough on the drying ground.
scenarios.body: Dicko The Legend sets a fair but manageable pace through the first three furlongs, and with no rival applying pressure, retains enough petrol to repel challengers inside the final furlong on good-to-firm ground that rewards resolution; Bayraat, tracking throughout, is best-placed to pounce if the leader flattens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Bayraat or a horse that secures a prominent tracking position overpowers Dicko The Legend in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bayraat has finished 1-2-2 in his last three starts at 6f on good ground and steps back to a trip where his finishing kick is sharp; racing just off the pace, he avoids the traffic nightmare facing the true hold-up brigade and has the clearest passage when the race ignites at the two-pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough, or a mid-race stumble in the lead group, creates a real gap for hold-up horses to exploit over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Applause and Saucy Jane both carry solid form at 5f on good ground and, of the redistributed hold-up contingent, are most likely to find clear daylight late; however, the overcrowded rear section means traffic problems are highly probable, capping the ceiling for this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Cramped, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If several hold-up horses interfere with one another mid-pack and the race devolves into a scrimmage, allowing a lightly-weighted or unexposed runner to slip through unnoticed.
scenarios.body: Koffee And Kale, a lightly weighted 3yo, has winning form at 5f and could thread through on a clean passage if the midfield bunches chaotically; Lieutenant Sir also showed a smart 6f win recently and retains upside, but the scenario requires a significant degree of positional fortune.

watchPoints.text: Bayraat is the most dangerous individual in the race: if he tracks Dicko The Legend cleanly from the start, he arrives at the furlong pole with a clear sightline and sharp recent form — watch whether Mr Eireann Cagney secures that second-position berth at the break.

Traffic is a genuine threat in the final two furlongs — with at least six hold-up horses compressed into midfield, any hesitation or switching will cost ground at the critical moment; Spirit Of Applause and Saucy Jane are most likely to find room, but watch the pack early for early crowding.

Dicko The Legend's stamina for 5½f must be monitored: all five recent runs in the form string are at 6f, and if the horse shortens stride inside the final furlong, the trailing pack will arrive in a wave — watch splits at the halfway point for any sign of deceleration.

Mister Moet's 97-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; Scott Dixon only has one runner in 22 days suggesting the horse may not be at peak sharpness, and any sluggish break from stall would extinguish whatever chance it holds.

The going is officially good-to-firm for this race despite the card headline reading "Good" — all seven races at Doncaster today have been returned good-to-firm, which slightly favours horses with proven fast-ground form (Bayraat, Spirit Of Applause) and marginally queries those who have shown their best on soft or easy going (Koffee And Kale, Donald).
